title: Evaluating a Deterministic Validator Plus Single‑Iteration Repair Pipeline for LLM‑Generated Network Configurations
abstract: We preregistered and executed a paired confirmatory experiment (N=300 paired intent→configuration tasks; preregistration id cand-2026-001-A-prereg-v1) to evaluate whether a minimal guarded pipeline—single‑shot LLM generation (declared model: gpt-5-mini) followed by a frozen deterministic configuration validator and at most one automated repair iteration—reduces first‑pass misconfiguration relative to plain single‑shot generation. Execution completed 600 episodes and used 301 model calls. Observed outcomes: baseline = 299/300 valid (99.667%); guarded = 300/300 valid (100.0%); paired counts n11=299, n10=1, n01=0, n00=0. Exact McNemar two‑sided p = 1.00; absolute paired difference = 0.0033333; paired bootstrap 95% CI = [0.00, 0.01] (10,000 resamples, seed 1729). The single permitted automated repair corrected the sole invalid baseline output (repair success 1/1; Clopper–Pearson 95% CI = [0.025, 1.0]). The preregistered planning assumption used for power calculations (planned baseline pass rate = 0.40) was contradicted by the observed near‑ceiling baseline, rendering the preregistered ≥50% relative‑reduction target effectively untestable. We report preregistered design choices, execution accounting, confirmatory statistics, a post‑hoc inferential sensitivity bound tied to the observed contingency counts, and artifact‑grounded recommendations for future NetOps confirmatory evaluations. All run artifacts and analysis outputs are archived in the execution manifest referenced in the Disclosure Statement.

sections.introduction: Translating operator intent into device configuration is a core NetOps function. Large language models (LLMs) can accelerate intent→configuration synthesis but are probabilistic and therefore risk omission, misordering, or unsafe commands. The community increasingly recommends hybrid guarded architectures that pair probabilistic generation with deterministic validators/simulators and bounded automated repair as operational safety nets. Despite this, rigorous preregistered evaluations that quantify the incremental effect of narrowly bounded guarded pipelines on first‑pass validity under controlled sampling semantics remain scarce. We address this gap with a preregistered paired experiment that isolates the incremental effect of a frozen deterministic validator plus at most one automated repair iteration on a single LLM candidate per task. Research question: Can this minimal guarded pipeline reduce the first‑pass misconfiguration rate of LLM‑generated network configurations relative to plain single‑shot generation under paired, shared‑candidate semantics?
sections.related_work: Recent demonstrations and surveys document promise and failure modes for LLMs in intent translation and NetOps workflows [10.1002/nem.2313; https://openalex.org/W4411015066; https://openalex.org/W4407163436]. Cross‑domain work shows verifier‑assisted and retrieval‑augmented pipelines reduce factual errors in clinical and software domains [10.36227/techrxiv.176784505.56675782/v1; 10.2139/ssrn.6608518], motivating guarded NetOps designs. Deterministic network verification algorithms (e.g., header‑space and specification checking) provide foundations for static validators that can check reachability and policy constraints without live execution [10.1145/3098822.3098834]. Surveys and architectural proposals emphasize generate→verify→repair with human oversight and provenance as critical components for safe agentic NetOps [10.6028/nist.ai.100-2e2023; 10.36227/techrxiv.177004277.71795055/v1]. Our study contributes a preregistered, artifact‑archived paired evaluation that measures first‑pass validity under an explicit validator+repair floor and documents operational tradeoffs tied to pairing semantics and baseline prevalence.
sections.methodology: Preregistration and hypotheses: We preregistered study cand-2026-001-A-prereg-v1 before execution. Confirmatory hypotheses: H1 — the guarded pipeline reduces first‑pass misconfiguration rate by ≥50% (relative) versus single‑shot generation; H2 — one or fewer automated repair iterations recover ≥75% of initially invalid configurations. The preregistration explicitly assumed a planning baseline pass rate = 0.40 (this assumption informed power calculations and is reported here because the observed baseline contradicted it). Design: paired within‑task sampling using a frozen deterministic task generator with N=300 seeds. For each seed a single shared LLM candidate was produced and used as the baseline response and as the starting point for the guarded arm (shared_initial_candidate semantics). This shared‑candidate pairing was preregistered to replicate the operational workflow of repairing a single proposed plan; it reduces cross‑arm generation variance but increases within‑pair correlation, limiting discordant pairs available to paired tests. Model and provider policy: declared model = gpt-5-mini. Execution accounting and model sampling determinism: execution used 301 model calls (300 initial shared generations + 1 repair invocation); these counts appear in the archived execution manifest. The frozen execution/model_configuration.json records declared_model_version = "gpt-5-mini" and temperature = null (artifact: execution/model_configuration.json, SHA-256 = 1acce92558edeb13cd97b75817329d332afe4a36d01d566f1a26c61b132923fa). Because temperature was unset (null) in the archived model configuration, explicit sampling determinism was not fixed in the prerun contract; therefore sampling determinism is unspecified in the execution artifacts and must be considered an operational uncertainty affecting generation variance. Validator, scoring, and repair: The deterministic validator canonicalized outputs to a normalized AST and applied per‑task workflow and dependency checks (required_sequence, expected_final_state, must_be_down_for_fields, final_group_constraints, minimum_active_in_groups). Scoring used full intent‑constraint validation: success required the normalized_configuration to satisfy the task constraints. The preregistered repair adapter is restricted to a single automated repair attempt per episode and receives the shared candidate plus structured violation codes; repaired outputs are revalidated by the same deterministic validator. Missingness and contamination: preregistered retry policy allowed a single infrastructure retry; primary analysis uses 'complete_pair_primary' (drop pairs only if both calls failed). Deterministic contamination checks (normalized AST exact equality and near‑duplicate lexical thresholds) were preregistered; no exclusions were triggered in the run. Statistical analysis: primary estimand = paired_success_rate_difference_guarded_minus_baseline; primary test = exact McNemar two‑sided at α=0.05; paired bootstrap percentile 95% CI (10,000 resamples, seed = 1729) was preregistered. Secondary analyses included binomial CIs for repair success and stratified checks. All artifacts, seeds, validator traces, repair prompts/responses, and analysis code are archived in the execution manifest and analysis bundle.
sections.results: Execution accounting (artifact‑derived): planned episodes = 600; completed episodes = 600; complete pairs analyzed = 300. Model calls used = 301 (300 shared initial generations + 1 repair invocation); repair_stage invocations = 1 (execution manifest entries and hashes record these counts). Primary outcomes (archived counts): baseline_success_count = 299/300 (99.667%); guarded_success_count = 300/300 (100.0%). Paired contingency derived from archived analysis artifact analysis/paired_contingency_table.csv (SHA-256 = 3421adb52d5791a979397368165fc2062e6b9a4a771ce49c0bcac80b02215d55): n11=299, n10=1, n01=0, n00=0. Inferential results (preregistered): exact McNemar two‑sided test yields p = 1.00 on the observed contingency. Observed absolute paired difference (guarded − baseline) = (n10 − n01)/N = 1/300 ≈ 0.0033333. Paired bootstrap percentile 95% CI = [0.00, 0.01] (10,000 resamples, seed = 1729; bootstrap parameters archived). Repair outcomes (H2): the single allowed automated repair corrected the sole invalid baseline output (repair success 1/1); Clopper–Pearson 95% CI for 1/1 = [0.025, 1.0], reflecting extreme imprecision from a single event. Why p = 1.00: exact McNemar conditions on the observed discordant total (n10+n01 = 1). With only one discordant pair, the null permutation distribution has minimal resolution and cannot produce a small two‑sided p‑value for this observed pattern; the paired bootstrap CI and the contingency artifact are the more informative numerical summaries in this low‑discordance regime. Post‑hoc sensitivity bound: the observed discordant total (1) imposes a hard upper bound on resolvable absolute paired improvement equal to 1/300 ≈ 0.00333. By contrast, the preregistered target (≥50% relative reduction from planned baseline 0.40) would require roughly 90 net discordant pairs favoring guarded outputs (absolute ≈ 0.30), showing why the preregistered large‑effect hypothesis was not testable with the observed baseline. Representative artifacts: per‑task validator traces include normalized_configuration, parsed_command_count, required_command_count, violation_codes, and repair_applied flags; these trace formats and selected per‑task entries are archived and form the authoritative source for the counts above (see execution manifest and analysis bundle).
sections.discussion: Interpretation tied to artifacts. The archived contingency (n11=299, n10=1, n01=0, n00=0) constrains inference: the absolute paired difference equals (n10 − n01)/N = 1/300, and the exact McNemar p = 1.00 is a direct consequence of conditioning on a single discordant pair. The preregistered planning assumption (baseline = 0.40) was contradicted by the observed baseline (0.9967), which removed statistical headroom to detect the preregistered ≥50% relative reduction. Design tradeoffs and operational framing. The shared_initial_candidate pairing models remediation of a single proposed plan (operationally relevant) but reduces informative discordance relative to independent draws; future preregistrations must align pairing semantics, targeted estimand, and power calculations. Practical design levers (artifact‑grounded): (1) calibrate task difficulty or adversarially augment tasks to produce a nontrivial baseline failure prevalence or a prespecified discordant count; (2) explicitly preregister pairing semantics and repair budgets and incorporate their effect on discordant expectations into sample‑size computations; (3) when runtime semantics matter, integrate emulation/simulation stages and preregister how emulator outcomes map to success/failure. Construct validity: our validator applies deterministic static checks and canonicalization rather than executing configurations in a runtime emulator; therefore results are conditional on the validator's static semantics and do not measure dynamic control‑plane or dataplane consequences. Repair evidence and precision: the observed repair success (1/1) demonstrates feasibility of automated correction for at least one failure mode, but the estimate is highly uncertain; studies designed to measure repair effectiveness precisely must ensure sufficient planned counts of initial failures. Reproducibility: the run demonstrates the value of full artifact archiving—seeds, normalized responses, validator traces, repair prompts/responses, paired contingency table, and analysis code—enabling independent recomputation of reported numbers and intervals (artifact paths and hashes are recorded in the execution manifest). Operational implication: when baseline error is already rare, guarded pipelines function more as catastrophic‑risk preventers (safety net) than as mechanisms for large throughput gains; organizations should align evaluation objectives accordingly.
sections.conclusion: We executed a preregistered paired experiment (N=300 pairs) comparing single‑shot LLM generation (declared model gpt-5-mini) to a guarded pipeline consisting of a frozen deterministic validator and a single automated repair iteration. Baseline single‑shot generation produced 299/300 valid outputs; the guarded pipeline produced 300/300 valid outputs. The lone initial failure was corrected by the single allowed automated repair, but the observed near‑ceiling baseline contradicted the preregistered planning assumption (baseline = 0.40) and removed headroom to detect the preregistered ≥50% relative reduction. Future confirmatory NetOps evaluations should (a) calibrate task difficulty or adversarial augmentation to secure sufficient initial failures or targeted discordant counts for planned effect sizes, (b) preregister pairing semantics and repair budgets explicitly, and (c) include emulation when runtime semantics are material to the operational claim. All raw outputs, validator traces, repair traces, the execution manifest (including model_calls_used = 301 and repair_stage invocations = 1), and analysis artifacts are archived and enumerated in the Disclosure Statement to permit reproduction of the reported counts and intervals.

limitations: Synthetic task bank and constrained vendor‑template scope limit external validity to broad production environments.
Single LLM (declared: gpt-5-mini) and a single validator implementation restrict generality across model families and validator designs.

The preregistered power plan assumed a baseline pass rate = 0.40; the observed baseline (299/300) contradicted that assumption and removed headroom to detect the preregistered ≥50% relative reduction.
Sampling semantics (shared_initial_candidate) reused the same initial candidate across paired arms, increasing within‑pair correlation and reducing discordant pairs available to McNemar inference.

Validation used deterministic configuration/constraint checks rather than full dynamic emulation of runtime semantic effects; actual runtime consequences of configurations were not executed and remain unmeasured.

H2 repair‑success evidence is based on a single initially invalid case (1/1 → 100%), yielding a wide Clopper–Pearson 95% CI = [0.025, 1.0]; larger counts of initial failures are required to estimate repair effectiveness precisely.
